faq.name: How does it work
faq.value:
Detector periodically queries AWS API and generates Alerts for problems found:

- `CloudWatch`: alarms (VPC, EC2, EKS and other services health)
- `CloudTrail`: management events (IAM changes, security groups, bucket policies, ...). Only write events by default: `track_event` adds all other events, including read-only (`Get*`, `List*`, ...), with `INFO` severity
- `IAM`: insecure IAM configuration (root access keys, missing MFA, old access keys)
- `S3`: buckets availability

faq.name: Cron
faq.value: Cron interval to check Cloud. Refer to [Cron](https://docs.extractor.live/common-configurations#cron) for more details

faq.name: URI
faq.value:
AWS URI: `aws://[ACCESS_KEY:ACCESS_SECRET[:SESSION_TOKEN]@][host]?param=value`

Credentials which are not in URI are read from environment (`AWS_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_ACCESS_SECRET`, `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`, `AWS_REGION`, `AWS_ACCOUNT`) or AWS default credentials chain. Prefer `auth` for authentication.

Examples:

`aws://?region=eu-west-1&account=123456789012`

`aws://?region=eu-west-1&states=ALARM,INSUFFICIENT_DATA&namespace=AWS/EC2,AWS/EKS` (CloudWatch)

`aws://?source=iam.amazonaws.com&events=CreateUser,DeleteUser&window=60` (CloudTrail)

`aws://?max_key_age=90` (IAM)

`aws://?buckets=my-bucket,my-bucket-2&latency=3000` (S3)

Alerts have `system` (generic: `Watch`, `Trail`, `IAM`, `Storage`), `sys` (AWS name: `CloudWatch`, `CloudTrail`, `IAM`, `S3`), `ref` (console link), `tx_hash` (CloudTrail EventId, alarm ARN, user ARN, bucket ARN).

faq.name: Auth
faq.value:
Optional authentication URI. It has a **preference** over credentials in `uri` (keys, `profile`, `role_arn`): if `auth` is specified they are ignored. `region`, `account` and custom host are still taken from `uri`.

Syntax: `scheme://body?param=value&param=value`

- `secret://<ACCESS_KEY_ID>:<SECRET_ACCESS_KEY>[:SESSION_TOKEN]` - static keys. `SESSION_TOKEN` is optional: if it is not specified, it is requested from the Cloud (AWS STS) and refreshed automatically. Never put real keys into the configuration: use `secret://{AWS_ACCESS_KEY}:{AWS_ACCESS_SECRET}` to take them from environment
- `env://[$ACCESS_KEY_ID]:[$SECRET_ACCESS_KEY]:[$SESSION_TOKEN]` - names of the environment variables (`$` is optional). Omitted names are default (`AWS_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_ACCESS_SECRET`, `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`). `SESSION_TOKEN` is never taken from the default variable if key or secret names are custom
- `profile://[file]` - profile from the credentials file (default: `~/.aws/credentials`), profile name: `?profile=name`, `AWS_PROFILE` or `default`. The profile can use `credential_process` (SSO): credentials are refreshed automatically
- `role://` - IAM role of the environment (ECS task, EKS pod, EC2 instance profile, web identity): credentials are refreshed automatically

Parameters (any scheme): `arn` (assume the role, credentials are refreshed automatically), `external_id`, `session`, `duration` (seconds), `sts=false` (do not request `SESSION_TOKEN`)

Examples:

`role://`

`role://?arn=arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/Sentry&external_id=abc`

`env://`

`env://$MY_KEY:$MY_SECRET`

`profile://?profile=sentry`

`profile:///etc/sentry/credentials?profile=sentry`

`secret://{AWS_ACCESS_KEY}:{AWS_ACCESS_SECRET}`

faq.name: Credentials refresh
faq.value:
Temporary credentials (`SESSION_TOKEN`, SSO) **expire** and a static `SESSION_TOKEN` is never refreshed while Detector is running. Credentials sources (in order of priority):

1. Keys in URI (`aws://KEY:SECRET[:TOKEN]@`)
2. `profile=NAME` - profile from shared credentials file (`~/.aws/credentials` or `profile_file=/path`). Profile can use `credential_process` (SSO, Vault, any external refresher), which is called again when credentials expire
3. Environment keys `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`/`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`/`AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`
4. AWS default chain (nothing specified): IAM role for ECS/EKS (IRSA)/EC2 - **recommended for production**, refreshed automatically

If keys (URI or environment) are specified **without** `SESSION_TOKEN`, the session token is requested from STS (`GetSessionToken`) and renewed automatically (disable with `sts=false`). If `SESSION_TOKEN` is specified it is used as is and **expires**.

Add `role_arn=ARN` (optionally `external_id`, `role_session`, `role_duration` seconds) to assume a role: credentials are refreshed automatically before expiration.

Examples:

`aws://?region=eu-west-1` (IAM role of the host/pod)

`aws://?region=eu-west-1&role_arn=arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/Sentry&external_id=abc`

`aws://?region=eu-west-1&profile=sentry`

faq.name: Condition
faq.value: Condition on the number of findings (per system) to generate Alerts. Default is `> 0`. Refer to [Condition](https://docs.extractor.live/common-configurations#condition-threshold) for more details

faq.name: Track New
faq.value: Alert only once on every new finding. If disabled, all active findings are reported on every check

faq.name: Track Events
faq.value: `Trail` only. By default Alerts are generated only for write (mutating) CloudTrail events: `HIGH` severity for security sensitive ones, `MEDIUM` for others. If enabled, Alerts are also generated for read-only events (`Get*`, `List*`, `Describe*`, ...) with `INFO` severity. Use `source` and `events` URI parameters to limit the volume

faq.name: Timeout
faq.value: Max time (milliseconds) to wait for Cloud API

faq.name: Track Error
faq.value: Track and alert on Errors (Cloud access errors, invalid credentials)
